comparison: Perfect agreement on lesion characterization (C36-C47). Both evaluations find the neuroimaging and histological methods robust and well-documented, with OpenEval noting 'converging evidence' and peer reviewers praising 'precise localization' and quantification methods.

Perfect agreement on downstream histological effects (C48-C50, C6-C8, C34, C107-C108, C145). Both find the evidence for degeneration and GABA changes convincing, with peer reviewers calling findings 'intriguing' and noting they 'support the idea of cortical structures exerting cognitive control over subcortical networks.'

Perfect agreement on preserved vocal production capacity (C2, C31, C51-C55, C57, C60-C61, C63, C137, C140-C142). Both evaluations emphasize this as an important negative result showing specificity, with peer reviewers noting 'no or little influence on certain aspects' and OpenEval highlighting the distinction between production and quality.

Perfect agreement on increased minor call types (C58-C59, C62). Both accept the statistical findings without challenge, though OpenEval notes the biological significance is unclear and the effect appears transient.

Strong agreement on selective reduction in social contact calls (C3-C5, C32-C33, C64, C78-C79, C105, C115). Both evaluations view this as a major contribution, with peer reviewers calling evidence 'convincing' and OpenEval noting 'converging evidence from multiple analyses.' Peer review includes additional claims about developmental trajectory and interpretation (C65, C84-C85, C104, C114, C121) not grouped with this finding by OpenEval.

Perfect agreement on preserved syllable count (C90-C93). Both accept this as an important negative result demonstrating specificity to call quality rather than structural organization, with no concerns raised by either evaluation.

Perfect agreement on control measures (C66-C67, C71). Both evaluations emphasize the importance of these controls for ruling out alternative explanations, with peer reviewers specifically praising their inclusion and OpenEval noting they strengthen interpretation of specific vocal deficits.

Strong agreement on main conclusions (C9, C109-C110, C136, C143, C154, C158). Both evaluations endorse these conclusions as well-supported, with peer reviewers calling evidence 'convincing' and noting the study 'strengthens the long-standing hypothesis.' Peer review includes C144 not in OpenEval grouping.

Partial overlap on acoustic features. OpenEval addresses syllable duration (C70, C94-C95, C103, C106, C122) as SUPPORTED. Peer review addresses broader acoustic changes (C94-C99, C101-C103, C106, C122) as UNCERTAIN, noting findings are 'intriguing' but functional interpretation requires experiments on conspecific responses.

OpenEval addresses increased mean frequency (C96-C97, C147) as SUPPORTED with strong statistics but notes transient nature is unexplained. Peer review groups this with other acoustic features (C94-C99, C101-C103) and rates as UNCERTAIN due to concerns about functional interpretation without conspecific response data.

OpenEval addresses reduced peak frequency (C98-C99) as SUPPORTED with robust statistics but uncertain functional significance. Peer review includes this in broader acoustic findings (C94-C99, C101-C103) rated UNCERTAIN, emphasizing need for experiments on how conspecifics respond to altered calls.

OpenEval addresses reduced entropy (C101-C103) as SUPPORTED statistically but notes uncertain functional interpretation. Peer review includes entropy in broader acoustic findings (C94-C99, C101-C103) rated UNCERTAIN, with concerns about translating acoustic measures to communication function without behavioral validation.

OpenEval rates transition pattern findings (C65, C84-C85) as UNCERTAIN due to marginal statistics (p=0.055). Peer review includes these claims in broader social call findings (C3-C5, C32-C33, C64-C65, C78-C79, C84-C85, C104-C105, C114-C115, C121) rated as SUPPORTED, suggesting acceptance despite borderline significance.

OpenEval addresses interpretations about social vocal development (C114, C116, C119, C121) as SUPPORTED but notes inference beyond direct observations. Peer review includes C114 and C121 in broader social call findings rated SUPPORTED, though separately questions functional interpretations in R11.

Both evaluations rate mechanistic interpretations (C118, C146, C148) as speculative/uncertain. OpenEval explicitly marks as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct experimental support. Peer review (R11) notes missing data on non-vocal social behaviors and questions whether mechanisms are alternate causes, rating UNCERTAIN.

Both evaluations question functional interpretation of acoustic changes. OpenEval rates claims about social message quality (C123, C131) as UNCERTAIN/speculative. Peer review (R8) explicitly states interpretation of 'deficient' social messages is 'still an assumption' without experiments on conspecific responses, rating UNCERTAIN.

OpenEval rates long-term implications and translational claims (C132-C133, C135, C159-C162) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are speculative without direct support. Peer review (R8) shares concerns about translational assumptions (C160-C161), questioning whether findings 'directly translate to marmoset communication.'

Both evaluations accept background claims about marmoset models (C1, C10-C17) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these establish appropriate rationale. Peer review implicitly accepts by affirming marmosets 'can provide insights into neural mechanisms underlying human speech' due to brain structure and social behavior similarities.

Both evaluations accept background claims about ACC function and connectivity (C18-C29) as SUPPORTED based on established literature. OpenEval notes extensive prior research support. Peer review affirms 'many previous studies show that ACC plays an important role in volitional and emotion-driven vocal behavior.'

OpenEval addresses normal developmental changes in temporal parameters (C68-C69) as SUPPORTED, noting these are important negative results. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

OpenEval addresses background on marmoset vocal development and ACC function (C72-C76, C80) as SUPPORTED based on prior research. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these background claims.

OpenEval addresses context from prior ACC lesion research and human prosodic deficits (C138-C139, C155-C157) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these comparative claims.

OpenEval addresses anatomical and functional circuit context (C149-C153) as SUPPORTED based on prior research. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these circuit mechanism claims.

OpenEval addresses normal developmental patterns (C111-C113, C120) as SUPPORTED, providing baseline for evaluating lesion effects. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these developmental baseline claims.

OpenEval addresses developmental changes in cry rates and parental feedback (C81-C83) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these cry-related developmental claims.

OpenEval addresses nuanced discussion of entropy interpretation (C124-C130) as SUPPORTED, praising acknowledgment of competing views and uncertainty. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this methodological discussion.

OpenEval addresses experimental design and sample size (C35) as SUPPORTED but notes relatively small n=5 per group. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses sample size concerns.

OpenEval addresses interpretations about motivation and social need (C119) as SUPPORTED but involving inference. Peer review (R11) questions whether altered vocalizations reflect motivation changes or are secondary to other social behavioral changes, rating UNCERTAIN and noting missing non-vocal social behavior data.
